widgets_values: 帮我把这张图转为儿童插画风格，色彩鲜艳

image1，Extract only the printed ink/design layer from the apparel photo and place it on a pure white rectangular canvas.
Think of the input as two layers:
1. ink/design layer: printed artwork that should remain
2. garment/photo layer: cloth, shape, lighting, and texture that must disappear
Keep the ink/design layer:
- central body artwork
- left and right sleeve prints when visible
- left and right shoulder prints when visible
- text, numbers, icons, badges, borders, stripes, bands, dots, line art, illustrations, decorative marks, and intentional distress attached to a design element
- sleeve stripe bands, parallel sleeve lines, cuff-adjacent printed bands, and simple geometric sleeve marks; these are printed artwork and must not be mistaken for seams or sleeve edges
Delete the garment/photo layer completely:
- shirt silhouette, body outline, neckline, neck opening, collar, V-neck triangle, sleeve shapes, shoulder/yoke panels, side panels, hem, cuff, seams, stitching
- fabric base color, mesh holes, knit/weave texture, cloth grain, folds, wrinkles, shadows, highlights, lighting gradients, background
- large pink/white/gray/black/blue/colored cloth fields and any fabric panel used as a carrier behind the print
- random dirt, loose splatter, ink wash, stains, mottled discoloration, and photo artifacts unless clearly attached to a printed design element
Output format requirements:
- pure white background everywhere cloth was removed
- no garment outline, no sewing-pattern pieces, no collar scrap, no shoulder panel shape, no sleeve panel shape
- print zones may be separated by white space, but their original left/right/up/down relationship should remain recognizable
- front views usually contain five visible zones: center body, left sleeve, right sleeve, left shoulder, right shoulder; keep all visible zones
- a sleeve zone may include both a large number/icon and one or more horizontal printed stripes or word bands; keep both
Do not create or redraw a new design. Do not rewrite text. Do not recolor, vectorize, simplify, or merge everything into one emblem. Preserve the source artwork's visible colors, outlines, relative scale, rotation, and placement. The result is wrong if it looks like a shirt, a flat garment pattern, or only the central body graphic.
